lookOutFor: Tough and quick, with scented flowers; it feeds the soil, as beans do.

cropping.notes: Pick the red berries when fully coloured.

lookOutFor: Scented early flowers for bees, and it feeds the soil, as beans do.

cropping.notes: Pick the strawberry-like fruits when soft.

lookOutFor: Grown mostly for its starry white flowers in June and red autumn leaves.

cropping.notes: Gather the fruits when their papery husks fall.

lookOutFor: Low and sprawling, earlier to crop than cape gooseberry.
source: Check against: RHS – ground cherry; nursery label

cropping.notes: Pick when dark red; the scent fills the room.

lookOutFor: An old wild strawberry with an extraordinary scent. Most need a male plant nearby.

pests.name: Slugs and snails
pests.signs: Young plants eaten, especially on damp nights
pests.control: Protect young plants and check for slugs after dark; encourage birds, frogs and beetles.

pests.name: Birds
pests.signs: Ripe fruit pecked or gone
pests.control: Net the plants as the fruit colours, or grow in a fruit cage.

source: Check against: RHS – musk strawberry; nursery label

cropping.notes: Pick the small black berries in autumn.

lookOutFor: A neat evergreen for acid soil, with late berries.

avoid: Lime, mushroom compost, wood ash and hard tap water: it needs acid soil. Water with rainwater.

source: Check against: RHS – evergreen huckleberry; nursery label

cropping.notes: Pick when yellow and fragrant.

lookOutFor: Red or orange flowers on bare stems in early spring, then hard, scented fruit.

steps.note: Round the base, as far out as the branches, then a mulch of compost.

source: Check against: RHS – japanese quince; nursery label

cropping.notes: Pick when fully coloured and slightly soft.

lookOutFor: A tree tomato for a greenhouse or conservatory; outside only in summer.

pests.name: Aphids
pests.signs: Green or black insects on leaves and roots
pests.control: Rinse off; encourage ladybirds and hoverflies.

pests.name: Whitefly
pests.signs: Tiny white insects under leaves, in greenhouses
pests.control: Yellow sticky traps and good ventilation; biological controls are available.

wintering.notes: Keep frost-free over winter.

steps.note: Under glass or in a pot.

source: Check against: RHS – tamarillo; nursery label

cropping.notes: Pick in their long husks as they turn brown.

lookOutFor: Like hazel, with the nut wrapped right inside a long husk. Plant two for a good crop.

steps.note: A mulch round the young tree.
